help.anchor: The reference date the fixed schedule counts from.
help.area_id: Optionally place the task in an area for grouping and filtering. Without one, it uses the attached device's area.
help.card_links: Documents or links from the attached appliance to surface on the dashboard card.
help.completion_detail: Ask for a note, a cost, or who did it when the task is completed.
help.consumable_link: Completing the task draws this part's per-use amount from stock and can fire a reorder alert.
help.consume_quantity: How much one completion takes off. Leave empty to use one whole spare.
help.create_buy_task: Adds a one-off "Buy" task while low and removes it once restocked. No automation needed.
help.device_id: Optionally attach the task to a device so it appears on that device's page.
help.due: When this one-off task is due.
help.freq: How often the fixed schedule repeats.
help.labels: Optional labels for filtering and notifications.
help.last_completed: When it was last done, so the task starts measured from then rather than from today. Leave blank to start from now.
help.name: A short name you'll recognize in the to-do list, e.g. "Replace water filter".
help.notes: Optional details: steps, part numbers, or anything handy when you complete it. Markdown is supported.
help.reading: What the sensor read when the work was done. Filled in for you. Change it if you are logging something you did earlier.
help.recurrence_type: How this task repeats. Pick after each completion, a fixed schedule, or just once, or let a sensor decide.
help.reorder_at: At or below this, a low-stock event fires. Automate on it, or enable Auto-create buy task below.
help.require_tag_scan: Blocks the Done button, so the task can only be completed by scanning its tag.
help.restock_quantity: Spares added back when you complete the Buy task. Enough to clear the threshold.
help.sensor.section: This task has no schedule. A sensor decides when it's due. Home Keeper notes the sensor's reading now and counts from there. Completing the task starts a fresh count. Learn more.
help.sensor_attribute: Optional. Read this attribute of the sensor instead of its main value.
help.sensor_baseline: The reading the count starts from, so a machine already part-way through an interval doesn't start over. Leave blank to count from what the sensor reads when you save.
help.sensor_clear_on_recover: Complete the task by itself once the condition goes away. Leave this off to mark it done yourself.
help.sensor_comparison: How the reading is compared to the threshold value.
help.sensor_entity_id: The entity that drives this task. It can be numeric (a usage meter or a measurement) or a binary sensor that reports on and off.
help.sensor_for: How long (seconds) the condition must hold before the task is due. 0 fires immediately.
help.sensor_mode: Usage / meter counts how far the sensor climbs. Threshold fires when it crosses a value. State fires when it changes to the state you pick.
help.sensor_state: The state the entity has to enter for the task to become due. A binary sensor reports On or Off.
help.sensor_target: Units of use before the task is due. Counting starts from the reading below, or from what the sensor reads now if you leave that blank.
help.sensor_value: The value the sensor's reading is compared against.
help.stock_unit: What stock is counted in: ml, metres, bottles. Leave empty to count whole spares.
help.tag_id: Pick a Home Assistant tag, or type a tag ID. Scanning it completes this task.
help.unit: The unit for the interval is days, weeks, or months.
hint.sensor.backstopAll: It waits until {every} have also passed since the last completion.
hint.sensor.backstopAny: It also becomes due every {every} since the last completion, whichever comes first.
hint.sensor.clearOnRecover: It clears itself once the sensor is back to normal.
hint.sensor.state: The task becomes due when the sensor changes to {state}.
hint.sensor.stateFor: The task becomes due when the sensor stays {state} for {seconds}s.
hint.sensor.threshold: The task becomes due when the sensor is {comparison} {value}.
hint.sensor.thresholdFor: The task becomes due when the sensor stays {comparison} {value} for {seconds}s.
hint.sensor.usage: This sensor reads {reading} now. The task becomes due at {due} (that's {target} of use), then every {target} after each completion.
hint.sensor.usageAlreadyDue: Counting from {baseline}, the sensor is already {consumed} past it, more than the {target} target, so the task comes due as soon as you save it.
hint.sensor.usageBaselineAhead: The starting reading ({baseline}) is above what the sensor reads now ({reading}). Home Keeper counts that as a meter reset and re-anchors to the live reading, so set it at or below the current value.
hint.sensor.usageFromBaseline: Counting from {baseline}, so {consumed} of {target} is already used and the task becomes due at {due}.
hint.sensor.usageFromBaselineNoReading: Counting from {baseline}, so the task becomes due at {due} (that's {target} of use).
hint.sensor.usageNoReading: The task becomes due once the sensor climbs {target} above its reading when you create the task, then every {target} after each completion.

notify.urgency_help: An Android channel keeps the settings it was created with, so give the channel a new name to change it. Critical urgency needs Critical Alerts allowed for Home Assistant on an iPhone.

settings.exclusions_note: apply only while the sync above is on
settings.heading: Problem sensor sync
settings.help: Sync binary sensors with the "problem" device class as tasks. A synced task stays active while its sensor reports a problem and clears automatically when the source integration resolves it. It can't be completed in Home Keeper. Exclude specific sensors, devices, areas, or labels below.
settings.shopping_help: Put every auto-created buy reminder on an existing to-do list, so it reaches your voice assistant and whatever list you already use. Tick an item off there and Home Keeper completes the reminder and restocks the part. A reminder that ends without being bought takes its line with it, and anything already ticked off is left alone. Leave empty to turn this off.
settings.shopping_list_entity: Sync buy reminders to this list
settings.sync_problem_sensors_help: A synced task clears only when the source integration resolves the problem, not when you tap Done. Reminders for one offer Snooze in place of Mark done.
tasks.empty: No tasks yet. Click {addTask} to create your first maintenance reminder.
tasks.intro.body: Home Keeper tracks recurring home upkeep. Tasks come in a few flavors, and you'll see them mixed in the list below:
tasks.intro.companion: From companions: contributed by other integrations and shown with a “Managed by …” chip.
tasks.intro.monitored: Monitored: armed by a sensor or condition and cleared automatically. Some can't be marked done by hand.
tasks.intro.recurring: Recurring: repeats on a schedule or after each time you finish it (filter changes, vet visits, batteries).
tasks.intro.title: Welcome to Home Keeper
